rationale: The Court is most likely to issue a Roberts opinion reversing (or vacating and remanding) on the ground that nonfinal but litigation-tested Gingles findings can supply a district-specific “good reasons/strong basis in evidence” for VRA compliance without creating a constitutional trap, while reaffirming strict scrutiny and narrow tailoring. Thomas (likely joined in part by Gorsuch) is the most probable dissenter insisting that Louisiana lacked the requisite district-specific evidentiary showing for this non-compact district and that ongoing §2 proceedings cannot do the work.
